bindings.label: Sudden chest tightness progressing to severe respiratory distress and cardiac arrest
A 52-year-old woman with a history of Sjogren's syndrome initially presented to a regional hospital with sudden chest tightness.

On day 3, she developed severe respiratory distress and cardiac arrest with severe ventricular arrhythmias refractory to conventional CPR; after tracheal intubation, she was supported with peripheral venous-arterial ECMO and intra-aortic balloon pump.

On day 4, due to worsening cardiovascular status and persistent electrical instability despite ECMO and IABP, she was transferred by helicopter to another hospital; on arrival, blood pressure was 83/64 mmHg on ECMO at 3.5 L/min and IABP, and bedside transthoracic echocardiography showed severely depressed global wall motion with LVEF approximately 10%.
High-sensitivity troponin T is markedly elevated
Endomyocardial biopsy shows diffuse myocardial necrosis, interstitial edema, fibrosis, and monocyte/multinucleated giant cell infiltration
Echocardiography shows global hypokinesis without regional wall motion abnormalities
Bedside echocardiography shows no right heart strain or aortic dissection features
